question: What is the maturity amount if ₹40,000 is invested for 2 years, the rate of compounded interest (compounded annually) being 8% for the first year and 10% for the second year?
solution:
Given:

₹40,000 is invested for 2 years, the rate of compounded interest (compounded annually) being 8% for the first year and 10% for the second year.

Concept used:

One year of compound interest on a certain sum of money is equal to the one-year of simple interest on the same amount.

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

According to the concept,

The amount becomes at the end of the first year

⇒ 40,000 + (40,000 × 8 × 1)/100

⇒ 40,000 + 3200

⇒ 43,200

The amount becomes at the end of the second year

⇒ 43,200 + (43,200 × 10 × 1)/100

⇒ 43,200 + 4320

⇒ ₹47,520

**∴ The maturity amount is ₹47,520.**

73:T
